transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because everybody keeps acting like I’m the one who’s not seeing things right—my husband, and people at the warehouse. But I know what’s going on. They’ve been watching what I do, like my moves at work, and messing with the pallet counts so I don’t get that supervisor spot. 

And it’s not like I don’t know how that place runs—I’ve been around freight and stock long enough, you can tell when numbers don’t add up. My husband just says I’m “making it bigger than it is,” but he wasn’t there when they started acting different around me.
Do you believe for certain that your coworkers are deliberately changing the pallet counts to harm you?

Yes. I mean, I’m not just saying it because I’m upset. I’ve watched it happen—people watching how I move around the warehouse, then the pallet counts come out wrong in a way that makes me look bad. And then everybody wants to act like I’m crazy for noticing it.

It’s about that supervisor spot, that’s what this is. They don’t want me getting it. My husband keeps saying I’m making too much of it, but he’s not there on the floor with me when they start acting strange.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

Sometimes, yeah… like, it’s not all the time. But I’ll be in one of the aisles at work, and I hear a man’s voice clear, like he’s right there, saying, “Nicole, check it again.” And then I look around and nobody’s near me.

It happened at home too, when I was folding clothes, which is why I know it’s not just warehouse noise or people talking by the loading doors. But then, you know, when the counts are already off and people are watching what you do, it makes you want to check everything twice anyway.
Have you felt as if thoughts were being put into your mind by someone or something outside you?

I don’t know if I’d say thoughts are being put in my mind exactly… it’s more like I can tell what they’re doing. My husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy for noticing, but they’ve been watching my moves, and then the pallet counts get changed around.

And see, that’s what I keep trying to explain—when you’re working freight, you know when something is off. I’ve been there long enough. They don’t want me getting that supervisor spot, so they make it look like I’m messing up. My husband just keeps saying I’m overthinking it, but he’s not the one on the floor seeing how they watch me.
How long have these experiences been going on?

About… eight months, I think. It’s hard to pin it down exactly because at first I thought it was just people being weird at work, you know, like warehouse stuff, people getting competitive. But the voices and that feeling like they’re watching me or changing things—it’s been going on around eight months now.

And it got worse once that supervisor talk started, because then everything felt connected to that. But yeah… about eight months.
Since this started, have you been having trouble keeping up with your work or taking care of things at home?

Yeah… I mean, I still go in, I’m not just sitting around doing nothing. But they took me off the forklift, which really bothered me, because I’ve done that work before and I know how to be careful. They said it was safety-sensitive and my counts were taking too long, my routines were slowing the line down.

And at home… my husband says he can’t rely on me like he used to. Like if something needs done, he acts like he has to double-check me now. Which, honestly, I don’t think is fair, because when you’re trying to keep things straight and people are rushing you, of course you’re going to slow down a little.
When you hear that man’s voice, does it happen often?

Yeah, it happens… not all day, but more than once in a while. Like sometimes I’ll be in the aisle at work, trying to get the counts right, or even at home folding clothes, and I’ll hear a man’s voice clear as day say, Nicole, check it again.

And then I do check it, because—well, you don’t want to be wrong and have people act like you’re the problem. But it’s strange because nobody will be near me when it happens. It’s not like someone standing right there saying it.
